x: Odell's win in the 100 yds. handicap from Scratch. The 880 handicap brought out the biggest field of the day, 31 actually competing of an original entry of 36.

Looking through the list of sufferers, one sees such names as McMullen and Odell (Irish); Williams, Davis, Davies, Thomas and Powell (Welsh); Fletcher, Mitchell, Crighton, Stewart and McKay (Scotch); and Merlin (Cornish).

In the 440 yards relay, Odell gave us a good lead over the first 100 yards and the advantage was never lost. The feature of the 2 miles relay was a fine " half " by Duffett, who wiped off a big deficit and handed over well ahead.

Lander ran the third stage and Odell finished a fast furlong with 10yds. to spare. Odell won the inter-club 100yds., but did not attempt to go "all out" in the handicap event in view of the relay race later in the evening.
Duffett (660yds.), Scammell (880 yds. walk), Odell (220yds.), (scr.) 1st.
The 110yds. men then had their second attempt to settle their race, Jarvis, Pollard, Port, Odell running for Belgrave, and Leigh-Wood, Cohen, Bourne and Basan for the L A.C.
Ernie Jarvis, Titherley, Pollard and Odell did duty for Belgrave and our sprint champion managed to gain the lead on the last stage and gave us first blood.
Let every stride beat "Odell's,"
Odell, H.
Odell regained the lead on the first furlong stage and handed over to Dunckley with a fair lead. Dunckley went right away from Hawkes, of Highgate, in the straight, and won easily.
Odell, with F.

In speaking of Seniors I wish my remarks to be taken generally, as we have, of course, sprinters of undoubted merit in Odell, Jarvis, Cook, Maryon and Pollard The main point is that generally we are in a bad way for sprinters.
In extenuation, we must point out that neither Odell nor Dunckley, the Club Champions at these distances, were available to run. The half-mile proved to be a very close race.

The 100 yards match event was won by our sprint champion, Odell, closely followed by Jarvis, with the Ashcombe champion, Harris, third. The quarter gave Jim Tosh an opportunity to stretch his legs and he returned 52 4-5 secs., being followed home by Beswick, of Ashcombe, and Harold Titherley, who wo…

Odell was close and his finishing burst gave him the title once again. It must give him satisfaction to know that he again equalled the championship record, for as crack sprinters go he is a sort of veteran, though not in age.
Then McKay, finishing with Odell, and this quartet are to be congratulated. Read has certainly strengthened our team.

Maurice Odell therefore won without serious opposition, but he did so in quite good time. He has won this championship seven times, and has held it continuously since 1925—a fine record for a sprinter.
Odell, A.
Odell 2, J.

A new holder was also produced in the next championship event to be decided—the 100 yards Senior. Morgan, the holder, did not turn out, and bearded old stagers like myself rather hoped that Odell would regain the title he lost last year.
